subject: Post-call: handling scoped PII & request for subprocessor evidence
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@healthsync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: handling scoped PII & request for subprocessor evidence

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Summary of ask (from your team):
- Confirm Redwood's position as Controller vs Processor for HealthSync workloads (scoped to HealthSync-supplied patient prompts and metadata).
- Provide current subprocessor roster and whether any subprocessor access logs can be produced on request.
- Confirm breach notification timeline and evidence chain (you asked whether Redwood can acknowledge incidents within 24–48 hours).
- Clarify retention options for PII-derived artifacts (inference logs, KV cache, and embeddings) and whether per-customer retention policies can be enforced.
- Data residency guarantee for US-only hosting for this workload.

What I can commit to now (pending legal/security confirmation):
- Redwood typically operates as Processor for customer-supplied inputs; we'll confirm precise wording for the DPA addendum.
- We can provide a full current subprocessor list and our SOC 2 report.
- Standard initial acknowledgement is 72 hours; we'll flag whether we can shorten that to 48 or provide a 24-hour acknowledgement step.

Requested items from HealthSync:
1) Can you attach the DPA language you prefer (we discussed sending your standard DPA).
2) Example of the types of logs you need (redacted sample or fields list) so security can validate feasibility.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- Today: you share DPA + log sample (Emma).
- By EOD next business day: Redwood privacy to confirm Controller/Processor wording and share subprocessors & SOC2 (Marissa).
- Schedule 30-minute security Q&A this week if you want deeper technical review (Rishi).

Attachments referenced: none from Redwood in this note.

If anything above is incorrect, flag and I’ll update. Happy to jump on a short call tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Emma Li <emma.li@healthsync.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthSync Legal <legal@healthsync.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: handling scoped PII & request for subprocessor evidence

Thanks Dylan — appreciate the clear recap. Attaching our standard DPA and a short sample log specification (fields we need).

A couple of clarifications from our side:
- HealthSync is the Controller for patient data; vendors act as Processors. We need explicit language in the addendum that clarifies this and that Redwood will not use HealthSync data for model training.
- Regarding breach notice: our procurement team prefers an initial acknowledgement within 24 hours and a substantive update within 72. If 24-hour acknowledgement is not possible, please confirm the fastest you can do.
- We require a per-customer retention toggle for inference logs (ability to set retention to 30/90/365 days).
- For residency: we need US-only hosting for this workload. Can you confirm available regions and whether we can pin to a US region?

Attachments: [Attachment: HealthSync_DPA_2027.pdf], [Attachment: HealthSync_LogSpec.xlsx]

We’re available for a 30-minute slot on Thu 6/17 at 10:00am PT or Fri 6/18 at 9:00am PT.

—Emma Li
Head of Privacy & Compliance
HealthSync
emma.li@healthsync.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: handling scoped PII & request for subprocessor evidence

Dylan — looped in. Background / legal stance for drafting:
- Redwood's standard position: we are a Processor when customers supply prompts and data; customers remain Controller. We will include a clause prohibiting training on customer-provided PII unless explicitly permitted by the customer.
- Subprocessors: we maintain an up-to-date roster and a notice process. I can share the current list and the CSV export (attached). Some subprocessors are cloud infra providers and inference-optimized partners; none have access to raw data outside of what the runtime needs.
- Breach notifications: our incident playbook supports a 72-hour substantive notification window. We can provide an initial acknowledgement sooner (24 hours) in most high-severity cases, but committing contractually to 24 hours for all incidents is operationally risky. Suggest the following compromise for contract language: initial acknowledgement within 48 hours, substantive update within 72 hours, and critical incidents flagged for immediate phone escalation.
- Retention: we support configurable retention policies per-customer for inference logs and embeddings. Embeddings can be configured to be ephemeral; we need to review how HealthSync wants deletion verified (audit logs +/- attestation).
- Residency: we have US-only deployment options (us-west and us-east regions) and can pin workloads to US-only hosts under Private or Dedicated plans. Hosted may require a region selection and written assurance; we’ll provide specifics.

I’ve attached: Redwood_Subprocessors_2027.csv and Redwood_SOC2_Report_2027.pdf.

Next actions I’ll take:
1) Draft suggested DPA addendum language that: clarifies Processor role, prohibits training on customer data, outlines subprocessors and notification cadence, and provides retention options.
2) Confirm technical approach to per-customer retention toggle and deletion verification steps — I'll pull in engineering if needed.

Dylan — if you can get HealthSync's preferred DPA back to me, I’ll mark up differences and propose redlines.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Privacy & Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Subprocessors_2027.csv], [Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2027.pdf]

From: Emma Li <emma.li@healthsync.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthSync Legal <legal@healthsync.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: handling scoped PII & request for subprocessor evidence

Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. I reviewed the subprocessor list and SOC2 at a high level; looks fine — procurement will do a closer review.

We can be flexible on the contract language if Redwood can commit to:
- An initial acknowledgement within 48 hours and a best-effort 24-hour ack for critical incidents.
- A per-customer retention setting that we can set at onboarding (30/90/365).
- US-only residency guarantee for this workload (we’ll accept hosting in the us-east cluster).

We’ll accept your proposed approach for the incident timeline as long as the DPA explicitly documents the phone escalation path for critical incidents.

Let’s take Thu 6/17 at 10:00am PT for the 30-minute security Q&A. I’ll send a calendar invite and include our security engineer.

Thanks,
Emma
Head of Privacy & Compliance, HealthSync
